Issued at 225 PM EDT Sat Aug 29 2026

Today-Tonight... Upper level high pressure over the Atlantic and the 
SW US will merge over the southern US and the Gulf today, as a 
trough across the eastern US, extending down across north Florida, 
continues to weaken. At the surface, high pressure over the Atlantic 
will continue to shift northward, moving north of the Florida 
peninsula as a quasi- stationary boundary draped across the 
southeastern US weakens and washes out overnight. Locally, winds 
will shift easterly today, both at the surface and gradually aloft, 
as that high pressure axis lifts northward. The east coast sea 
breeze is forecast to form this afternoon, with the onshore flow 
aiding the sea breeze to push farther inland through this afternoon. 
Moisture across the local area will remain above normal, with PW 
values of 1.8-2.2". This will support scattered to numerous showers 
and storms this afternoon. Scattered storms have already formed and 
pushed onshore across the south, with some showers and storms 
forming around the I-95 corridor this afternoon. Local guidance 
continues to show additional isolated to scattered showers and 
storms forming along the sea breeze, with coverage anticipated to 
increase as the sea breeze pushes inland. Highest coverage of 
storms will occur across the interior, mainly across Lake and 
western Orange and Osceola counties, in association with the sea 
breeze collision late this afternoon and into this evening. 

The environment supports storms this afternoon, with plenty of 
instability (MUCAPE 1700-2500 J/kg), ample buoyancy (lifted index
of -6 to -8), and adequate downdraft potential (DCAPE 700-1000 
J/kg). Main storm hazards will be frequent to excessive lightning,
gusty winds of 45-55 mph, and heavy rainfall of 1-3", which may 
lead to minor localized flooding in urban and poor drainage areas.
The Weather Prediction Center (WPC) has outlined all of east 
central Florida into a Marginal Risk (level 1 of 4) for Excessive 
Rainfall. Any lingering activity will diminish shortly after 
sundown, with activity across the Atlantic waters continuing 
through the overnight hours. Some of this activity may push 
onshore through the night. Temperatures will be near to slightly 
above normal, with afternoon highs in the upper 80s to low 90s 
along the coast, and low to mid 90s across the interior. These 
temperatures coupled with humidity will produce peak heat indices 
of 100-107F, which remains below Heat Advisory criteria. 
Conditions tonight will remain warm and muggy with overnight lows 
in the low to mid 70s. 

At the beaches, a moderate risk of rip currents is forecast due to a 
developing long-period swell and the onshore flow. Always swim near 
a lifeguard and never enter the ocean alone. Heed the advice of 
local beach safety officials and posted flags.

Sunday-Friday... Upper level high pressure over the southern US will 
slowly shift eastward through the time period. At the surface, broad 
high pressure will remain in place, with the ridge axis staying 
north of the Florida peninsula. At the surface, high pressure over 
the Atlantic will remain in place, with the ridge axis staying north 
of the Florida peninsula. Locally, deep easterly flow will prevail, 
with speeds generally around 10 mph. this will support the 
development and farther inland progression of the east coast sea 
breeze each afternoon. Moisture across the local area will remain 
near to above normal, with PW values of 1.8-2.1". Daily afternoon 
showers and lightning storms are forecast to continue, with 
scattered storms forming each day along the advancing east coast sea 
breeze, with additional showers and storms forming across the 
interior. Highest coverage of storms will be across the interior, 
where the sea breeze collision is forecast to occur each evening, 
generally around Orlando westward. Storm hazards will be frequent 
lightning, gusty winds, and locally heavy rainfall. Shower and 
lightning storm activity will diminish into the overnight hours, 
however, scattered showers and storms will continue across the 
Atlantic waters each night. Some of this activity may push onshore 
along the coast in the easterly flow through the night and into
the morning hours each day. 

Temperatures will remain seasonably hot and humid with highs in 
the upper 80s to low 90s along the coast and low to mid 90s across
the interior. These temperatures coupled with high humidity will 
produce heat indices of 100-106, with up to 108 possible in spots 
next week. A Heat Advisory may be needed for some parts of east 
central Florida next week. Be sure to stay adequately hydrated if 
spending extended periods of time outdoors and also take breaks in
the shade or in air conditioning to help prevent the development 
of heat-related illness. Overnight lows will continue to be warm 
and muggy with lows in the low to mid 70s.
